title: Chapter 51 — Trade Outreach: The Builder Cold Call & First Contact
intro: The research-first standard and the opening that earns thirty seconds, per buyer type.

sections.title: Research Before You Call
sections.content:
Never cold call a builder without knowing their work. Google them. Check their website. Look at their current projects on Google Maps or permit databases. Understand their tier — are they building $300K starter homes or $2M custom homes? The opening is completely different.

For custom builders: 'Hi [name], I have seen your work on [project/neighbourhood] and the quality is impressive. I specialize in premium appliance packages for custom homes and I would love to show you how we support our builder partners.'

For volume builders: 'Hi [name], I know you are building [number] homes in [area]. We have a builder program with standardized packages, priority delivery scheduling, and dedicated support. Can I send you our spec sheets?'

For renovation contractors: 'Hi [name], I noticed you are doing a lot of kitchen work in [area]. We support about 15 renovation contractors with same-day quoting and flexible delivery. Can I show you how that works?'

sections.title: Channel Strategy
sections.content:
Phone call for builders — they are on job sites and respond to calls. Leave a voicemail if they do not answer — mention their specific project by name so they know you did your homework.

Email for designers — they work at desks and respond to visual presentations. Attach a beautiful spec package, not a price list.

LinkedIn for architects — professional context. Connect with a personalized note referencing a specific project.

Job site drop-by for contractors — bring your card and a spec sheet. 'I was in the neighbourhood and wanted to introduce myself.' This works because contractors respect people who show up.

sections.title: The Goal Is One Meeting
sections.content:
The goal of first contact is not to close. It is not to pitch. It is to earn a meeting. One meeting. That is all.

'Would you be open to a 15-minute meeting to see if we could help on your current projects? I will bring spec packages at three price tiers and we can see if there is a fit.'

If they say no, ask when would be a better time. If they say they are happy with their current supplier, say: 'I respect that. Would you be open to a backup option in case anything changes? I would love to introduce myself for the future.' Plant the seed. Move to the quarterly touch cadence. Wait for the incumbent to stumble.
